Four-panel diagram showing the steps of charging by induction. Panel 1: A negatively charged rod is brought near a neutral metal sphere on an insulating stand. The sphere shows '+' charges on the side near the rod and '-' charges on the far side. Panel 2: A wire connects the far side of the sphere to an earth symbol; electrons (arrows) flow down to the earth. Panel 3: The earth wire is removed while the rod is still held near the sphere. Panel 4: The rod is removed, and the '+' charges distribute evenly over the whole sphere. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

A cross-sectional view of a gold-leaf electroscope. A flat metal cap at the top is connected to a vertical metal rod. The rod passes through an insulating rubber stopper into a transparent glass jar. At the bottom of the rod inside the jar, there is a fixed vertical brass plate and a thin gold leaf hinged at the top, diverging at an angle away from the plate. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

Four panels showing electric field flux patterns. Panel 1: An isolated positive charge '+' with straight arrows pointing outwards. Panel 2: An isolated negative charge '-' with straight arrows pointing inwards. Panel 3: A positive '+' and negative '-' charge side by side. Arrows originate from the '+' and curve smoothly over to end on the '-'. Panel 4: Two positive charges '+' and '+' side by side. Arrows point away from each charge and bend sharply upwards and downwards away from the center line to avoid each other. A large 'N' marks the empty neutral point in the center. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.
